angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 460,553 km at 62.89 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.9000 +/- 0.0308 mas (same row, RUWE 1.55): 62.89 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.662 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Leleu et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-178 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.211L/abstract): 460,553 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.647 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Leleu et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-178 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.211L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4316 +/- 70 K from Leleu et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-178 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.211L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Leleu et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-178 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.211L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-178.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.607, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-178 (pscomppars): spectral type K, from Leleu et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021A&A...649A..26L/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, WT 2353: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-178 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.23 dex, from Leleu et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.211L/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-178 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.86646, from Leleu et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.211L/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-178 (pscomppars): age 6 Gyr, from Leleu et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...688A.211L/abstract)
